materials.title: 建议、规则与药品名词

questions.prompt: Choose the correct advice about a note.
options: She should to bring the note.
questions.evidence: She should bring the note.
questions.explanation: should 后接动词原形，不随 she 加 s。

questions.prompt: Choose the correct negative advice.
options: He should not guesses the number.
He should not guess the number.
He should not to guess the number.
He not should guess the number.
answers: He should not guess the number.
questions.evidence: He should not guess the number.
questions.explanation: should not 后用动词原形 guess。

questions.prompt: Choose the correct question.
options: Do I should bring my card?
questions.evidence: Should I bring my card?
questions.explanation: 疑问句将 should 放在主语前，动词用原形。

questions.prompt: The sign requires visitors to check names. Choose the correct sentence.
options: You must to check your name.
questions.evidence: You must check your name.
questions.explanation: must 后接 check 原形。

questions.prompt: The sign prohibits entry. Choose the correct sentence.
options: You must not enters the staff room.
You not must enter the staff room.
You must not to enter the staff room.
You must not enter the staff room.
answers: You must not enter the staff room.
questions.evidence: You must not enter the staff room.
questions.explanation: must not 表示禁止进入。

questions.prompt: What does “must not enter” mean in the example?
questions.evidence: You must not enter the staff room.
questions.explanation: must not 表示不允许，并非仅仅不需要。

questions.prompt: Choose the correct sentence about one visitor.
options: The visitor has to signs the form.
The visitor have to sign the form.
The visitor has sign to the form.
The visitor has to sign the form.
answers: The visitor has to sign the form.
questions.evidence: The visitor has to sign the form.
questions.explanation: 第三人称单数用 has to，后接 sign 原形。

questions.prompt: Which phrase means “not necessary,” rather than “prohibited”?
questions.evidence: do not have to
questions.explanation: do not have to 指不必；must not 指禁止。

questions.prompt: Choose the sentence with uncountable medicine.
options: There are some medicine in the picture.
There is a medicines in the picture.
There is some medicine in the picture.
There are two medicine in the picture.
answers: There is some medicine in the picture.
questions.evidence: There is some medicine in the picture.
questions.explanation: 这里 medicine 指药物这一物质，搭配 some。

questions.prompt: Which phrase names two separate items?
questions.evidence: Two tablets are in the picture.
questions.explanation: tablet 是可数名词；two 后使用复数 tablets。

questions.prompt: Choose the singular countable sentence.
questions.evidence: A tablet is one item.
questions.explanation: a tablet 表示一片；单数主语用 is。

questions.prompt: Choose the correct phrase.
questions.evidence: She asks for advice.
questions.explanation: 本课 advice 为不可数名词，不用 an advice 或 advices。

materials.instructions: 阅读中文讲解及例句，再独立完成十二题并根据证据订正。
materials.passage:
1. should / should not 表示建议或不建议，后面用动词原形，不随第三人称加 -s：She should bring the note. He should not guess the number. 这是交流安排的例句，不是诊疗建议。疑问句可将 should 提到主语前：Should I bring my card? 易错：不说 should brings，也不加 to。

2. must / must not 与 have to 表示规定。You must check your name. You must not enter the staff room. The visitor has to sign the form. must not 表示禁止；do not have to 表示不必，两者意思不同。第三人称单数用 has to；must 后用原形。上面是虚构场所规则，不推断所有诊所相同。

3. 本课 medicine 表示药物这一物质时作不可数名词：There is some medicine in the picture. A tablet is one item. Two tablets are in the picture. 不说 two medicines 表示两片；如果说不同种类，可根据语境使用 medicines，但不把种类等同片数。advice 通常不可数：She asks for advice.

materials.title: A Clear Note for a Clinic Visit

questions.prompt: Why does Lena speak to the receptionist?
options: She wants to cancel her appointment.
She needs to find the dentist.
She needs to correct her appointment time.
Her phone number has an incorrect digit.
answers: Her phone number has an incorrect digit.
questions.evidence: Lena notices that the last digit of her number is wrong, so she asks the receptionist to change it.
questions.explanation: 她发现电话号码最后一位不对，因此请接待员修改。

questions.prompt: What has Lena written on separate lines?
options: The appointment details she wants to confirm.
The symptoms she wants to describe.
answers: The symptoms she wants to describe.
questions.evidence: Lena has written one symptom on each line of a small card.
questions.explanation: one symptom on each line 明确说明卡片记录的是症状。

questions.prompt: Why does she leave the temperature part empty?
options: She has not measured her temperature.
She already knows she has a fever.
The nurse has already filled it in.
The form asks her to record it at a later visit.
answers: She has not measured her temperature.
questions.evidence: She has not measured her temperature today, and she does not know whether she has a fever.
questions.explanation: 她尚未测体温，因此不猜测。

questions.prompt: What does the poster invite visitors to write down if relevant?
options: The time and room number of the appointment.
The medicine labels of other patients.
An allergy and a previous injury.
The names and contact details of all clinic staff.
answers: An allergy and a previous injury.
questions.evidence: It suggests writing down an allergy and any previous injury if these are relevant.
questions.explanation: if relevant 表示在有关时记录过敏和既往伤情。

questions.prompt: What does the poster suggest bringing when someone has a medicine question?
options: The medicine label or a tablet package.
A card with the appointment time.
A prescription from a previous visit.
answers: The medicine label or a tablet package.
questions.evidence: The poster asks visitors to bring the medicine label or a tablet package if they have a question.
questions.explanation: 海报建议有疑问时带药品标签或药片包装，以便向专业人员询问。

questions.prompt: What does Lena understand about the poster?
options: A word on it is not a diagnosis.
answers: A word on it is not a diagnosis.
questions.evidence: She knows that a word on a poster is not a diagnosis.
questions.explanation: 词语本身不能诊断个人情况；她准备向工作人员询问。

questions.prompt: According to the passage, who is specifically mentioned as answering questions about a medicine label?
options: The nurse shown in the poster.
questions.evidence: She can ask the clinic staff for advice about her own situation, and a pharmacy can answer questions about a label.
questions.explanation: 句子将标签问题与 pharmacy 对应。

questions.prompt: Where will David wait?
questions.evidence: Please wait near the blue door.
questions.explanation: Lena 的信息明确约在蓝色门附近。

questions.prompt: Why is David visiting another building?
options: He is buying medicine for Lena.
questions.evidence: He is visiting a dentist in another building, not the clinic.
questions.explanation: David 去另一栋楼看牙医，并非在诊所工作。

questions.prompt: What is Lena’s plan for the conversation?
options: Choose her own diagnosis from the poster.
Describe what she notices and listen carefully.
Give the nurse a treatment plan.
answers: Describe what she notices and listen carefully.
questions.evidence: Her plan is to describe what she notices and listen carefully rather than decide what the words mean for her health.
questions.explanation: rather than 表示她不自行判断词语对自身健康的意义。

materials.instructions: Read the passage and choose one answer for each question.
materials.passage:
On Monday, Lena has an appointment at the Oak Street clinic at 10:15. She arrives early and goes to reception. A notice asks each patient to check that their name and phone number are correct. Lena notices that the last digit of her number is wrong, so she asks the receptionist to change it. The receptionist gives her a form and says that she can wait in the quiet room.

Lena has written one symptom on each line of a small card. Her list includes a cough and a sore throat. She also wants to mention a headache and pain in her shoulder. She has not measured her temperature today, and she does not know whether she has a fever. Rather than guessing, she leaves that part of the form empty. There is room for her to add a question about her stomach, too.

In the waiting room, Lena reads a poster about how to prepare for a conversation with a nurse. It suggests writing down an allergy and any previous injury if these are relevant. A visitor may also ask about a prescription or a treatment they do not understand. The poster asks visitors to bring the medicine label or a tablet package if they have a question. It suggests asking a professional what the word dose means on that label.

The poster shows a patient speaking with a nurse during an examination. In the picture, the patient asks what the word infection means. Lena also wants to understand the words people use in the clinic. She knows that a word on a poster is not a diagnosis. She can ask the clinic staff for advice about her own situation, and a pharmacy can answer questions about a label. She writes both questions down because she does not want to forget them.

Her friend David has agreed to meet her outside afterwards. He is visiting a dentist in another building, not the clinic. Lena sends him a short message: “My appointment is at 10:15. Please wait near the blue door.” David replies that he will bring a book while he waits. He remembers that Lena sometimes forgets her card when she is in a hurry.

Before her name is called, Lena looks at her list again. She adds questions about how to recover and when she might return to her usual routine. She has had less sleep than usual and wants to talk about a quiet afternoon of rest. She searches for words to describe feeling ill without saying that she already knows what is wrong. In the past, a walk in the park helped her feel healthy, and she wonders how to describe that. She plans to tell the nurse whether it is difficult to breathe while sitting quietly, then puts the card in her bag. Her plan is to describe what she notices and listen carefully rather than decide what the words mean for her health.

materials.title: A Different Clinic Visit

questions.prompt: When is Leo’s appointment?
questions.evidence:
Is your appointment still on Thursday, Leo?
Leo: Yes, at two forty in the afternoon.
questions.explanation: Leo 先确认星期四，再说下午两点四十分。

questions.prompt: Where is reception?
questions.evidence: It is beside the green entrance.
questions.explanation: green entrance 是接待处位置，yellow bench 是稍后的会合地点。

questions.prompt: What does Leo want the desk to check?
options: The time of Mara’s dentist visit.
questions.evidence: The patient form is available there, and I can ask them to check the spelling of my name.
questions.explanation: 他想请接待处核对自己姓名的拼写。

questions.prompt: What will Leo not guess?
questions.evidence: I will not guess a temperature or say I have a fever if I have not measured it.
questions.explanation: 没有测量时他不会猜体温或断言发热。

questions.prompt: What does Leo plan to explain about the pain?
options: Its location and when he first noticed it.
When the pain stopped and how much the medicine cost.
Which part of the form records his appointment.
answers: Its location and when he first noticed it.
questions.evidence: I will describe where it is and when I first noticed it.
questions.explanation: where 和 when 分别对应位置及首次注意到的时间。

questions.prompt: Where is the pharmacy?
questions.evidence: There is a pharmacy across the street.
questions.explanation: across the street 表示街对面。

questions.prompt: Why will Leo show the tablet package at the pharmacy?
options: To ask whether the package contains enough tablets.
To ask whether the medicine needs a prescription.
To ask the pharmacy to arrange his next appointment.
To ask what the label means.
answers: To ask what the label means.
questions.evidence: I will show the tablet package and ask what the label means.
questions.explanation: Leo 想把药片包装交给专业人员看，询问标签的含义，不是自行决定用药。

questions.prompt: What does Leo want to know about his allergy question?
options: Where his medicine label can be explained.
When his appointment will take place.
How long Mara should wait by the bench.
questions.evidence:
Did you write down your allergy question as well?
Leo: Yes. My main question is what information they need.
questions.explanation: Mara 问过敏问题，Leo 说主要想知道诊所需要什么信息。

questions.prompt: Where will Mara meet Leo?
questions.evidence: Please meet me by the yellow bench at three thirty, not at the green entrance.
questions.explanation: 句子明确纠正不是绿色入口，而是黄色长椅旁。

questions.prompt: What will Leo do if the meeting time changes?
options: Meet Mara at the green entrance instead.
Ask the dentist to move Mara’s visit.
Leave a note at the reception desk.
questions.evidence: I will text you if the time changes.
questions.explanation: text you 表示时间改变时给 Mara 发消息。

materials.instructions: Listen to the two speakers and choose one answer. Use this dialogue rather than the reading passage.
materials.transcript:
Mara: Is your appointment still on Thursday, Leo?
Leo: Yes, at two forty in the afternoon. I checked it this morning because I had written down two different times.
Mara: Where is the reception desk in that building?
Leo: It is beside the green entrance. The patient form is available there, and I can ask them to check the spelling of my name.
Mara: Have you prepared your questions?
Leo: I have a small list. I want to describe a cough, a sore throat and a headache. I will not guess a temperature or say I have a fever if I have not measured it.
Mara: Good. What about the pain you mentioned yesterday?
Leo: I will describe where it is and when I first noticed it. I also wrote down a question about my stomach. The nurse can ask for any other information during the examination.
Mara: Is there a place to ask about a prescription?
Leo: Yes. There is a pharmacy across the street. I have a question about a word on a medicine label, but I will ask the professional there rather than guess.
Mara: Which word is it?
Leo: Dose. I will show the tablet package and ask what the label means. I will not decide what to take from the word alone.
Mara: Did you write down your allergy question as well?
Leo: Yes. My main question is what information they need. I will ask the nurse how to describe how I breathe and when I might recover. I will also ask for advice about my treatment.
Mara: I can wait for you after my dentist visit.
Leo: Thanks. Please meet me by the yellow bench at three thirty, not at the green entrance. I will text you if the time changes.

materials.title: Prepare for a Clinic Conversation
materials.instructions: Read the example aloud for practice, then record your own response with different details.
materials.prompt: Describe a fictional clinic visit and how you would prepare questions. Explain the appointment, the information you would check, and what you would ask a professional to clarify. Speak for 90–120 seconds, use at least six different lesson words, and avoid giving treatment or dosage advice.
materials.reference: I have an appointment at a community clinic next week. Before I go, I will write down the symptom I want to describe and the time I first noticed it. At reception, I will check my name and phone number. If I have a question about an allergy, I will put it on the same card. I might also ask a nurse what an examination involves. If a prescription has a word I do not understand, I can ask the pharmacy to explain the label. I will listen to the professional and take notes instead of guessing. My friend will wait outside, and I will send a message when the conversation is finished.

materials.title: A Note Before a Visit
materials.instructions: Write your own first draft using your own details. Do not copy the speaking example.
materials.prompt: Write 120–160 words to a friend about a fictional non-urgent clinic visit. State the appointment time and place, describe the information you will bring, explain two questions you want to ask staff, and arrange where to meet. Use at least six different lesson words. Do not provide a diagnosis, treatment plan, or dosage.

guidedOutput.title: 写作结构提示
guidedOutput.text: Write four parts: appointment details; information to bring; questions for the professional; meeting arrangement. Useful frames: I should bring ... / I have to check ... / I would like to ask ... .
